items.title: #Magic coach Sean Sweeney said Anthony Black (right ankle sprain) and Noah Penda (right hamstring strain) both had good practices today. Sweeney said Jalen Suggs (illness) did more and looked more like himself.
items.author: Jason Beede
items.body_excerpt:
#Magic coach Sean Sweeney said Anthony Black (right ankle sprain) and Noah Penda (right hamstring strain) both had good practices today. Sweeney said Jalen Suggs (illness) did more and looked more like himself.

"But for any of those guys, you can't skip steps," Sweeney said.

items.title: #Magic coach Sean Sweeney said Anthony Black (right ankle sprain) and Noah Penda (right hamstring strain) were both full participants in Friday’s practice and are doing well.
items.author: Jason Beede
items.body_excerpt:
#Magic coach Sean Sweeney said Anthony Black (right ankle sprain) and Noah Penda (right hamstring strain) were both full participants in Friday’s practice and are doing well.

Jalen Suggs (illness) is still under the weather but he’s been getting some shots up, Sweeney said.

items.title: #Magic coach Sean Sweeney said both Anthony Black (ankle) and Noah Penda (hamstring) were able to practice Sunday and do more in terms of the ramp-up stuff.
items.author: Jason Beede
items.body_excerpt:
#Magic coach Sean Sweeney said both Anthony Black (ankle) and Noah Penda (hamstring) were able to practice Sunday and do more in terms of the ramp-up stuff.

“They look good,” Sweeney said. “Hopefully they came out clean.  Looks like they did.”

items.title: The same goes for #Magic forward Noah Penda (hamstring), according to Orlando coach Sean Sweeney.
items.author: Jason Beede
items.body_excerpt:
The same goes for #Magic forward Noah Penda (hamstring), according to Orlando coach Sean Sweeney.

“They’re both pretty close to being back and ready to go,” Sweeney said about Penda and Black.

quote.author: Jason Beede
quote.text:
#Magic coach Sean Sweeney said Anthony Black (sprained ankle) has “definitely made progress” throughout the week. Black has done non-contact work at a “high, full-speed level as of today.”

“So, we feel pretty good about where he's at,” Sweeney said.
